description.narrative:
The specific objective (outcome) of the Action is: maturity and exposure of the Albanian start-up and innovation ecosystem and its stakeholders are increased.
Output 1 puts capacity development (CD) interventions for stakeholders of the Albanian start-up ecosystem at centre stage. Already existing actors and services will be strengthened to deliver qualitative and sustainable services. New public and private actors will be encouraged to enter the Albanian start-up and innovation ecosystem to complement current services.
Output 2 will improve and diversify finance opportunities for Albanian start-ups and Innovation Support Organizations (ISOs). GIZ will provide grants and capacity development to ISOs. Selected activities in the areas of crowdfunding, angel and equity investment complement this approach on GIZ side.
Output 3 promotes and implements the Quadruple Helix (QH) approach to generate innovation and economic growth. The target group is opened also to younger generations. Paradigmatic activities include green / circular project pilots on community level, awareness raising events and skills development programmes, e.g., via progressively integrating entrepreneurship education into university curricula.
Output 4 puts the spotlight on ecosystem promotion nationally and internationally, through big-scale events, campaigns and activities that aim to give needed attention and focus to the developing innovation ecosystem in Albania. The Action will design awareness raising campaigns and activities to promote key actors within the ecosystem, who can serve as ambassadors and role models.
Sida is responsible for the action output 2, focused on improving and diversify finance opportunities for Albanian start-ups through Innovation Challenge Fund. Challenge Fund grant scheme 2 , would provide funding to innovative Micro, small- and medium-sized enterprises (MSME - start-ups with innovative solutions), and start-ups with a prominent tech content, with the potential to go global and grow fast. Building a vibrant innovation ecosystem by increasing the number of start-ups across the country that are supported and empowered to model and market innovative ideas, expand or diversify their businesses pushing innovation further in Albania is within the focus of CF.

Denna utvärdering görs inför andra fasen av projektet EU4innovation. Fas 1 av projektet genomfördes mellan Oktober 2018 till December 2022. Under projektets första fas har Sida haft en betydande roll för att stödja innovationsekosystemet i Albanien. Detta genom att skapa och genomföra ”Innovation Challenge Fund”, som är baserad på svenska erfarenheter. Fonden har varit relevant för och svarat till behoven hos 40 albanska startupbolag, innovationsstödjande organisationer, och företag. Detta genom att tillhandhålla det stöd som saknas i deras tillväxtfaser, då det saknas liknande finansieringsmöjligheter för dessa typer av affärsidéer i Albanien. Fonden fyllde alltså en lucka i finansieringen av innovativa idéer och bidrog på så sätt till tillväxten av innovativa företag i hela landet, med engagemang från nystartade startupbolag och företag som leds av kvinnor, samt de som annars inte skulle ha kunnat omvandla sina idéer till affärsverksamhet. Till följd av dessa positiva resultat, och en förfrågan från Albaniens regeringen om att fortsätta bidra till ett stärkt innovationsekosystem, planerades det för och beslutades om en andra fas av projektet. Projektet "EU4Innovation" kommer att finansieras genom EU:s föranslutningsinstrument (IPA III) 2021–2027 för Window 4: Konkurrenskraft och inkluderande tillväxt; Tematisk Prioritering 2: utveckling av den privata sektorn, handel, forskning och innovation. I linje med de på förhand fastställda mål och resultat som anges i insatsdokumentet är det övergripande målet (effekten) för insatsen att öka Albaniens konkurrenskraft och socioekonomiska återhämtning efter Covid-pandemin genom att förbättra företagsklimatet, innovationsekosystemet och investeringsklimatet. Denna insats samfinansieras gemensamt av EU, the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) och Sida och genomförs av GIZ (output 1-4) och Sida (huvuddelen av output 2) under perioden december 2022 till maj 2026 (42 månader). Den totala budgeten för insatsen beräknas uppgå till 11 750 000 euro. EU åtar sig att ge ett bidrag på upp till 10.000.000 euro, BMZ upp till 1.200.000 euro och Sida upp till 550.000 euro. Av EU-bidraget på 10.000.000 euro får Sida totalt 2.350.000 euro. Projektet har GIZ som genomförandepart (output 1-4) och Sida ansvarar huvudsakligen för att handlägga Innovation Challenge Fund (den största delen av output 2). Innovation Challenge Fund 2 kommer att bevilja bidrag (med medfinansiering) till innovativa startupbolag och små till mellanstora företag. En miljon euro kommer att beviljas i bidrag, varav 0.8 miljoner euro finansieras av EU och 0.2 miljoner euro finansieras av Sida. Bidragsbeloppen kommer att vara mellan 10.000 euro och 30.000 euro. Bidragets storlek kommer att avgöras utifrån en bedömning av i vilket skede i sin livscykel som bolagen befinner sig i. Inledningsvis planerade ambassaden att genomföra insatsen med hjälp av en ledningsgrupp och en grupp av partners från implementeringen av projektets första fas. Planen var att projektet skulle drivas från ett separat kontor bredvid ambassaden, och skulle bemannas av en ledningsgrupp om fyra personer. Externa experter/konsulter skulle anlitas av Sida på behovsbasis. Baserat på de rekommendationer som inkommit från Utrikesdepartementets och Sidas inspektion 7-11 november 2022 så kommer en ny genomförandestuktur för EU4Innovation att inrättas. Ambassaden kommer att genomföra projektet via en extern genomförandepart. Projektets nya genomförandeupplägg kommer att beslutas om under övergångsperioden under det första halvåret av 2023.

This appraisal is done for the project EU4Innovation (Phase II), which is the continuation of the first phase of the project “Eu for Innovation” implemented from October 2018 - December 2022. During EU for Innovation phase 1, Sida has played an important role in boosting the innovation ecosystem in Albania, through creating and implementing Innovation Challenge Fund based on Swedish experience. The fund, has been relevant and responsive to the needs of 40 Albanian start-ups, innovation supporting organisations and enterprises through the provision of the missing support in their validation and growth phases, in absence of similar government or donor funding facilities to support such business ideas in Albania. Therefore, the Fund filled a gap in financing of innovative ideas, and in this way contributed to the growth of innovative businesses across the country, with engagement of women-led start-ups and businesses as well as those who would not have otherwise been able to transform their ideas into actual business activity. Following the positive outcomes, and the request from the government of Albania to further strengthens the innovation ecosystem, a second phase of the project was planned and agreed.EU4Innovation (Phase II), is financed by the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA III) 2021-2027 for Window 4: Competitiveness and inclusive growth; Thematic Priority 2: private sector development, trade, research, and innovation. In line with the pre-defined objectives and results outlined in the Action document, the overall objective (impact) of the Action is to increase the competitiveness and post-COVID socio-economic recovery of Albania through improvement of the business environment, innovation ecosystem and investment climate.This Multi Donor Action is jointly co-financed by the European Union (EU), the Federal Ministry of Economic Co-operation and Development (BMZ) and Swedish International Development Agency (Sida). The Action will be implemented by GIZ (the Lead Organization) and Sida (the Partner) between December 2022 to May 2026 (42 months). The total estimated budget of the action is 11. 750. 000 EUR. The EU will provide a contribution up to EUR 10.000.000, the BMZ up to EUR 1.200.000 and Sida up to EUR 550.000.The funds will be sent directly from EUD to GIZ, and then GIZ will forward the funds to Sida. Out of the 10.000.000 EUR from EU contribution, Sida will benefit a total of 2.350.000 EUR.GIZ is responsible to implement (output 1-4) and Sida is responsible to manage the Innovation Challenge Fund (main part of output 2). Innovation Challenge Fund 2, will award grants (with co-finance %) to innovative start-ups and Micro, small- and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). 1 Mio. EUR will be given in grants. (0.8 Mio. funded by the EU, and 0.2 Mio. funded by Sida). Grants amounts will start from 10'000 EUR – up to the maximum fund 30'000 EUR depending on the stage at which the start-ups are in their lifecycle.Initially, The Embassy of Sweden in Tirana planned to implement the action, through a management team, and a group of partners following the experience from implementation of EU for Innovation phase 1. The Challenge Fund was planned to be managed through a separate project office located next to the Swedish Embassy in Tirana and staffed by a management team of four persons. Additionally, external experts/consultants (contractors) would have been sub-contracted by Sida on a needs-basis.Based on the recommendations received from the inspection conducted by Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs and Sida during 7-11 November 2022, a new implementing set up for EU4Innovation project will be established. The Embassy of Sweden in Tirana will implement the action through an outsourced implementing partner, the new set up will be decided during transition phase of the 1st six months of 2023.

description.narrative:
By the end of the action, the expected result is: (i) a total of 50 innovative MSME and start-ups as the main target group and direct beneficiaries of Innovation Challenge Fund, have received financial and tailored capacity building support; (ii) Challenge Fund as an innovative and versatile finance mechanism have strengthened capacity for innovation in Albania; (iii) Challenge Fund institutionalized within the governmental system.
During the reporting period (01January 2023 - 31 December 2025) under Sida management, the Action successfully selected 55 startups across three calls for proposals, chosen from a pool of 637 applicants. This highlights both the high demand for support and the dynamism of the countrys growing entrepreneurial ecosystem. Notably, 51% of the selected companies are led by women, and the winners rep-resent 11 municipalities, demonstrating that the program is fostering more inclusive innovation and expanding opportunities beyond the capital, Tirana. At the same time, relevant Albanian innovation actors have strengthened their capacities. The newly established Startup Albania Agency (SAA), after receiving legal and financial expertise, has developed internal regulations, procedures, and financial frameworks critical steps for building a transparent and accountable public authority and for reinforcing the foundations of a sustain-able innovative ecosystem. Amendments have also been made to the startup law, introducing innovation and green growth instruments in line with EU regulations. As a result, an interim benchmark under the Growth Plan was met, which in turn unlocked 9 million euros from the Growth Facility for the Western Balkans.
Results achieved and main activities carried out during 2023-2025:
- The implementing partner, namely Partners Albania for Change and Development that will assist the Embassy of Sweden in Tirana to follow and execute the technical, administrative, and financial implementation of the Challenge Fund activities, has been selected and is on board.
- Challenge Fund Grant Scheme guidelines were prepared. A set of crucial documents for the sub-granting scheme were either revised or newly created from the beginning, such as: (i) Application forms for Lot 1, Lot 2, and Lot 3 (ii) Financial form (Budget template) (iii) Business Model Canvas template (iv) Indicative Action Plan Form (v) Guideline for Applicants document (vi) Application Instructions etc.
- The existing Challenge Fund online application platform (established during 1st phase of the project 2018-2022) underwent significant improvements. The main functionalities regarding application and evaluation module were redesigned and updated, along with enhancing user-friendliness. The updated platform ensures that the process from application to evaluation is automatically captured and stored in a systematic, standardized, and auditable way. Challenge Fund grant scheme supported three subcategories of start-ups as follows: Lot 1: Idea and validation stage start-ups, i.e., a founder or a team in the early stages of developing an innovative business idea (not registered in QKB). This category will be awarded up to maximum EUR 10,000 with minimum 5% co-financing from the applicant. Lot 2: Growth stage start-ups, i.e., a registered business entity (MSME) within the first 12 months of operation (from the official registration of the business entity at QKB to the date of publishing the Call for Proposals). This category will be awarded up to EUR 20,000 with minimum 20% co-financing from the applicant. Lot 3: Scale-up stage start-ups, a registered business entity (MSME) within the first 13 months to 5 years of operation (from the official registration of the business entity at QKB to the date of publishing the Call for Proposals). This category will be awarded up to EUR 30,000 with minimum 30% co-financing from the applicant.
- Regarding the CHF Launching and Application process, the fund launched three calls for proposals during 2023/2024/2025. A total of 637 applications proposals were received in total from 35 municipalities across Albania, with 48% submitted by women and 52% by men. Following the evaluation process, 55 startups were awarded funding.
- The first Call for Proposals of the CHF was launched on November 17, 2023, and remained open until December 22, at 6:00 pm. At the end of the application process, 247 applications were received, from which: Lot 1: 117 applications, Lot 2: 48 applications, and Lot 3: 82 applications. Of these, 46% were submitted by women and 54% by men. - The second Call for Proposals of the CHF was launched on May 9, 2024, in Europe Day events, and remained open until June 21, 2024, at 3:00 pm. By the end of the application process, 149 applications had been submitted, out of which: Lot 1: 68 applications, Lot 2: 24 applications, and Lot 3: 57 applications. Of these, 48% were submitted by women and 52% by men. - The third Call for Proposals of the CHF was launched on February 7, 2025, at Innovation Hub at the Pyramid of Tirana and remained open until March 17, at 3:00 pm. 241 applications were received, out of which: Lot 1:117 applications, Lot 2:48 applications, and Lot 3: 76 applications. From 241 applications received, 48% of the applicants were women.
To support outreach and engagement, a total of 36 public information sessions were conducted for both calls, consisting of thirty (30) onsite events and six (6) online sessions. These sessions took place across 17 municipalities, including Tirana, Elbasan, Vlora, Korça, Berat, Saranda, Kukës, Fier, Pogradec, Lezhë, Shkodra, Peshkopi, Përmet, Krujë, Durrës and Gjirokastër. The sessions successfully engaged approximately 1,246 participants, including start-up owners, MSMEs, students, academic researchers, and service providers within the ecosystem.
Moreover, the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) section was published on the CHF website (https://challengefund.euforinnovation.al/), where all questions received were summarized and made publicly available. Throughout the promotion and the open application period of both Call for Proposals, a total of 140 Q&As related to the application process were published. Additionally, a standardized e-mail was sent from the official CHF e-mail address (challengefund@euforinnovation.al) to all individuals who submitted inquiries, providing instructions on where to find relevant answers.
Out of the 55 grants awarded, 25 were allocated to Lot 1 - Idea and Validation stage; 15 to Lot 2 Growth stage, and 15 to Lot 3 - Scale-up stage. The grants have been distributed across several municipalities, including Tirana, Kamëz, Berat, Librazhd, Shkodra, Divjakë, Malësi e Madhe, Korca, Saranda, Vlora, and Durrës. The grants are categorized into various sectors such as ICT Sustainable Agriculture/Food; Tourism; Circular Economy; Health Care and Wellbeing; Education Technology; Recycling/Upcycling; Fintech Industry; Textile; Agrotourism Green and Digital Transition and Business Services. The implementation period for grant contracts ranges from six to twelve months, depending on the scope and nature of the funded activities. The total funding allocated to the 55 grant beneficiaries amounts to EUR 970,000.
-Evaluation of the feasibility of the handover process of CHF to Albanian institution completed.
Tailored capacity-building and technical assistance are being provided to all CF beneficiaries, covering financial, legal, and promotional aspects. During the reporting period, supported start-ups received personalized training, mentoring, and coaching tailored to their specific business ideas.
-Start-up beneficiaries under the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Calls for Proposals received grant management training on 18 June 2024, 16 January 2025, and 9 October 2025, respectively; covering contract implementation, reporting requirements, procurement procedures, expenditure documentation, and applicable financial regulations.
- A five day training programme titled Doing Business Management of the Entrepreneur-ship Initiative was implemented to strengthen the managerial and entrepreneurial capacities of startup founders in Albania. The programme consisted of three thematic modules: Module 1: Mastery of Doing Business Introduced core entrepreneurial concepts and enhanced participants practical business management skills. Module 2: Financial Literacy and Man-agement Provided essential knowledge on financial planning, management practices, and decision making tools, enabling participants to manage business finances effectively and im-prove their ability to access funding. Module 3: Legal and Fiscal Framework for Doing Business in Albania Improved participants understanding of the national legal, fiscal, and regulatory environment, with a specific focus on trademarks and the trademark registration process. Training sessions were organized in three cohorts corresponding to Calls for Proposals (CfPs): 1st CfP: 827 July 2024; 2nd CfP: 2028 May 2025, 3rd CfP: 27 October 19 November 2025. In total, 106 participants from supported startups completed the training. Overall, the programme offered vital insights and skills to navigate and thrive in the Albanian business landscape and support-ed startups in developing more sustainable, compliant, and investment ready business mod-els.
- Training on Cybersecurity Awareness for Albanian Startups addressing EU standards on data protection and digital resilience was held on 21 November 2025. The session delivered by Cyber Morfosis (a CHF grant beneficiary) equipped 20 startups with essential competencies, covering data protection and privacy principles (aligned with GDPR), and risk assessment, identification of prevalent cyber threats, baseline security policies and best practices, and the formulation of practical mitigation plans.
-Mentoring and coaching, the CHF is providing mentoring and coaching to all start-ups through individual needs assessments and a network of national and international experts. Between August 2024 and December 2025, an individual needs assessment was carried out for each of the 55 start-ups, resulting in comprehensive reports detailing their specific challenges, requirements, gaps, and customized recommendations and operational processes. A total of 39 experts were selected through a procurement process to form a mentoring network, consisting of 23 national mentors and 16 international mentors. The mentoring process for the first Call for Proposals (CfP) was implemented between December?2024 and March?2025. Mentoring for the winners of the second CfP was carried out during the period June-August?2025. The matching table for mentors and startups under the third CfP has been finalized based on the needs assessment results, and the mentoring scheme to be completed in 2026. The matching of mentors with startups was carefully conducted based on the startups identified needs and the mentors' fields of expertise. Each startup was paired with 23 mentors who addressed their most critical needs.
Regarding International Study Visits with Grantees and GoA representatives (3 study visits in Albania and 2 in European countries)
-The first international study visit was successfully organized and held in Stockholm, Sweden, from 25 to 27 March 2025, bringing together key Albanian stakeholders including winners of the 1st CfP and representatives from public institutions such as Ministry of Economy, Culture and Innovation, Startup Albania State Agency, Agency for Innovation and Excellence and Po-lis University, to explore Swedens dynamic innovation ecosystem. Designed to promote knowledge exchange and institutional cooperation, the three-day program included meetings with leading Swedish innovation actors such as Business Sweden, Swedfund, Vinnova, Sida, Almi, Stockholm University, Ignite Sweden, and KTH Innovation. The visit focused on three main themes: ideation and commercialization, scaling startups into SMEs, and internationali-zation. Participants gained insights into funding mechanisms, public-private partnerships, green entrepreneurship, and academic commercialization.
-The second international study visit was successfully organized and held in Barcelona, Spain, from 9 to 11 December 2025, bringing together key Albanian stakeholders including winners of the 2nd and 3rd CfP and representatives from public institutions such as Startup Albania State Agency. program included meetings with leading Catalonian innovation actors such as Barcelona Activa, Barcelona Chamber of commerce, 4YFN initiative (Four years from Now) (Fira de Barcelona), ACCIÓ, Barcelona Impact Hub, Barcelona Travel Hub & Tech Tour-ism Cluster, Barcelona Health Hub (BHH), Mediktor, Ocean Ecostructures, BlueTech Port, Barcelona Finance Hub & AtticoLab, and the startups Agrikola AI & Identify App. The programme was organized into three thematic blocks: first, public policies and institutional sup-port, focusing on how public institutions create an enabling environment for innovation; sec-ond, innovation hubs, accelerators, and clusters, highlighting the role of ecosystem builders in connecting key actors and accelerating growth; and third, innovation on the ground, exploring startup financing, digital entrepreneurship, and impact-driven ecosystems, with particular attention to the blue economy and technology-driven sectors.
Regarding the provision of capacity building support to the Start-Up Albania Agency,
-Legal and financial expertise was provided to SAA from May 2024 to January 2025. The legal support focused on delivering technical assistance that strengthened SAAs institutional, regu-latory, and operational frameworks. Key deliverables included the drafting and consolidation of internal regulations, HR procedures, and resource management guidelines; the development of intellectual property protection strategies and data security protocols; proactive legal risk management; the provision of ad hoc legal support; and the updating of regulations and doc-umentation for upcoming Grant Scheme Calls for Proposals. On the financial side, the agency received financial expertise and developed a comprehensive financial plan to support budget management and risk mitigation, ensure compliance with government regulations, and facili-tate the implementation of the 2024/2025 Grant Scheme.
-A training programme for the agencys staff was conducted online from June to September 2024 by the Norwegian company, Strategy Tools, with the participation of 13 staff members from the agency. The training programme featured six core thematic workshops, supplement-ed by comprehensive materials, access cases from established ecosystems, ad hoc support, and individual consulting sessions with the SAA director. Key topics included: understanding ecosystems, their evolution over time, and different ecosystem types; building and scaling startups; startup ecosystems and clusters; the venture capital ecosystem; the role of innova-tion agencies; and a wrap-up session focusing on future directions and next steps.
-Sida successfully collaborated with the MoSEBC and the Start-Up Albania Agency to transfer the CHFs methodology, covering both the application and evaluation processes. Throughout 2024, three activities were implemented, where the CHF methodology, digital platform, and guidelines were introduced to the ministry (MoSEBC) and the Start-Up Albania Agency. These activities encompassed the introduction of the methodological framework, the demonstration of the digital platform, and the presentation of the corresponding operational and procedural guidelines. Additionally, supplementary criteria on gender equality, environmental protection, and inclusivity for underserved areas incorporated in the application process were presented. Furthermore, several key elements of the CHF grant scheme including its application and evaluation procedures have been incorporated in the grant scheme manged by the Start-Up Albania Agency.
-On May 8th, 2025, a final workshop was held at the premises of the Startup Albania State Agency, at the Pyramid of Tirana. SAA presented the digital platform developed prior to the platform official launch, and the session focused on the functionalities of the online grant ap-plication platform and the full evaluation cycle, from application intake to the announcement of winners. This event was done as part of the ongoing support provided to the Agency in adopt-ing and integrating transparency measures into its platform, contributing to a more efficient and transparent startup support framework in Albania.
-Preparation and Publication of the Albania Startup Ecosystem Assessment Report Support was also provided to SAA to assess and formulate evidence based policies and tar-geted interventions aimed at advancing the Albanian innovation and start up ecosystem. In this context, an assessment of the national start up ecosystem was undertaken, resulting in the countrys first comprehensive report Albania Startup Ecosystem Assessment Report, produced in collaboration with Startup Genome, a world-leading innovation ecosystem development organization that prepares and publishes the Global Startup Ecosystem Report annually, offering authoritative insights into global startup ecosystems. The report highlights that, despite Albanian startup ecosystem remaining in an early activation phase with limited experience and resources, its strong local Connections, founder quality, emerging international links, and support programs such as SAA, EU4Innovation and EBRD, present significant untapped potential to position the country as a dynamic innovation hub in the Western Balkans. The report was officially launched and presented on 20 November 2025, during Global Entrepreneurship Week 2025. A total of 52 participants took part in the event.
- On the context to strengthen the skills and capabilities of the SAA staff, between July and December 2025, two technical support services were procured to strengthen the Albanian Startup Agency (SAA). The first supported the enhancement of SAAs digital platform through the development of a virtual entrepreneurship course for early-stage startups and capacity building for SAA staff to strengthen advisory services and startup support. The second engaged legal and financial experts to develop standardized startup documentation on company creation, governance, and financing, facilitating investment and partnership transactions with local and international stakeholders.
-Support was offered to SAA and the Ministry of Economy and Innovation for the amendment of Law No. 25/2022 -On the support and development of startups and innovation. including preparation of the related Decisions of the Council of Ministers and internal regulations required for the effective operationalization of the new innovation support instruments as foreseen in the Growth Plan. These amendments introduced EU aligned innovation and green economy measures, fulfilled an interim benchmark under the Growth Plan, that will result in the release of €9,025,310 million for Albania from the Growth Facility for the Western Balkans.
During the reporting period, around 500 posts and articles with visual images, stories and short videos were published across CHFs website, Instagram, and Facebook. These publications contained information about the EU support, the fund, a Calls section with details on current and past calls, guidelines, fact sheets for the Calls for Proposals, success stories, press trips, and application links. Additionally, updates were provided on launch events, schedules of information sessions and project activities, frequently asked questions about the application process, award ceremonies, publication of the list of start-up winners, and introductory posts for each beneficiary following their award. To ensure widespread dissemination of the first and second call for proposals of the CHF, a promotional spot was developed and presented during the launch events. The spot was broadcasted on the YouTube channel of EU4I and aired on national TV channels, including Top Channel, KLAN TV, and RTSH. The spot received an impressive 83,966 views, on CHF Instagram showcasing the high level of engagement with the CHF. Furthermore, the spot for the third call for proposals have been uploaded and shared on the CHF's Instagram platform reaching 35,500 views. A series of targeted promotional campaigns were carried out, boosting a total of 51 stories about start-ups winners and other CHF key events on Meta platforms, including Facebook and Instagram. These campaigns reached 889,916 accounts, with each account viewing the ads between 1.2 to 4.44 times. In addition, work is underway to develop and showcase 16 success stories of the start-up winners who have benefited from the CHF. 10 stories have been prepared with the remaining expected to be completed in March 2026. These success stories will be shared and promoted throughout 2026 to highlight the positive impact of the CHF, showcase successful beneficiaries, and acknowledge the support received from the EU. Recognizing the significance of communication beyond promotional activities, Sida has facilitated 35 key events with stakeholders, innovators, founders, and investors to foster connections and drive actions. These events provided opportunities for start-up visibility, knowledge exchange, networks expansion, and access to funding. (i.e. Tirana International Fair, Future 2Tech, GEW (global entrepreneurship week) 2023/2024/2025, networking activities, INNFEST2025, Breakfast with the Swedish Ambassador, awarding ceremonies, pitching events, national study visit, start-ups product launch events, etc). The CHFs dissemination and communication strategy included events-based outreach, ensuring engagement with key stakeholders in the start-up and innovation ecosystem and media representatives. As a result, a total of 95 news/feature stories and web articles were creat-ed for the CHF events and broadcasted on national television, as well as published in widely circulated print and online media. The CHF-supported startups were also highlighted as winners or success stories by other ecosystem actors, including government entities, television ), press media. European Union in Albania. These recognition were further promoted by the CHF through reposting these features in the project SM platforms, thereby expanding their reach and visibility. As well a Press Trip was organized on November 6th, 2025, in Divjakë and Berat. During the trip, journalists had the opportunity to visit four Challenge Fund beneficiaries Biolive, Rinora, Crystal Team (winners of the 1st CfP), and Sugo.al (winner of the 3rd CfP) and engage directly with their experiences. Nine journalists from various audiovisual and print media were invit-ed and had the opportunity to interview the founders of the four startups and later share their insights and the outcomes of the trip on their media platforms. The coverage was published and broadcast by a range of media outlets, including RTSh (Radio Televizioni Shqiptar), Scan TV Monitor Magazine, GazetaSi.al, Balkanweb, Trailblazing Magazine, AlbaniaWeb (which also shared the news on related platforms such as KASH.org.al, Fjala.al, and Argumentum.al), Vizion Plus TV (link 1, link 2), and News24 TV. To further enhance the visibility of the CHF beneficiaries, start-up winners received promotional support. This support involved assistance in organizing their launch events or product launches and feature posts and reposts on the CHFs social media accounts. In addition, for events organized by the start-ups themselves, visibility has been further enhanced by publishing their activities on CHF social media platforms or through communication platforms such as the Embassy of Sweden in Tirana and the CHFs cooperation partner Partners Albania for Change and Development.Through the CHFs communication platforms, people have been able to witness innovation in action, demonstrating how entrepreneurship can drive positive change and economic growth.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
